Why change projects stall

A company starts a change with a solution: a new structure, new values, a new system. Nobody has checked what the real problem is, people do not see why it is needed, and after three months everything quietly returns to the old way. Organizational development works in the opposite order: first diagnosis, then a plan agreed with the people involved, then the intervention and an honest evaluation.

What changes after this course

You agree the scope and the roles before the project begins. You collect data with interviews, surveys and observation and bring the findings back to the client. You build an action plan and choose interventions for the individual, the team and the process. You measure what changed. And you can lead the people who carry the change.

What is inside: 400 tools, counted file by file

You do not have to take this number on trust. Open any lecture and read its description: every tool inside is listed there by name.

Who is teaching

I am Mike, the #1 HR instructor on Udemy, with 1,800,000+ course enrollments from 170,000 students, and the author of about 200 books on Amazon. Your colleague said "yes", and nothing happened. Your feedback was polite, and the person was hurt. Open a lecture, take the model or the checklist, use it in your next call with a colleague from another country.

Why smart people misread each other

Everyone speaks English on the call, so it feels as if everyone means the same. They do not. In one culture "interesting idea" is praise, in another it is a polite no. One team expects the manager to decide, another expects to be asked. One person is offended by a direct remark, another does not notice a soft one. Nobody is wrong, and the project still slows down, because each side judges the other by its own rules.

What changes after this course

You can place a culture on a few scales: how directly people speak, how they give criticism, how they decide, how they build trust, how they treat time. You hear a refusal behind a polite phrase. You change the way you give feedback and argue a point depending on who is in front of you. And your team has written agreements on meetings, decisions and deadlines.

A company measures what is easy to count. People start working for the number, and the result the number stood for gets worse. Recruiters paid for the number of interviews hold more interviews.
